title: LWFA: Blockchain-Based Forensic Assurance Across the Digital Forensic Investigation Lifecycle
content: Many blockchain-based forensic systems focus on evidence integrity and chain of custody, but integrity alone does not establish whether an investigation result includes the information needed for independent review. Examination records, analyses, findings, and reports may be revised or challenged, so reviewers need to trace a conclusion’s derivation, assess its supporting context, and examine challenges. A report can contain hash-consistent evidence yet omit an analysis limitation, reference a finding version different from the report’s basis, or exclude an earlier challenge. We propose Lifecycle-Wide Forensic Assurance (LWFA), which links results to exact versions of supporting evidence, examination records, and analyses through declared dependencies; reconstructs required review information from recorded history rather than the presenter’s inventory; and preserves reviews, challenges, responses, and authorized dispositions, including later developments. Hyperledger Fabric smart contracts enforce recording rules; an off-chain verifier reconstructs obligations from a trusted reference peer. Across 18 scenario families, the study-specific Hash-CoC baseline did not flag seven of 11 seeded defects, five outside its scope; LWFA flagged all 11. The median paired verifier runtime increase over Hash-CoC was 89.0 ms; history replay was measured separately. Completeness remains relative to recorded history, scope, and policy.
